correctness.rationale: For every d>=2 and 1<=j<d, reduction to g=min(j,d-j) and h=d-2g is exact. Symmetric raw coefficients have center S and are bounded by S; expected-length palindromes force zero carries by outer-in induction. A carry bound of 27 excludes long palindromes for g>=3 and g=2,h>=1 through the impossible 2-digit palindrome ac. For g=1,h>=3 the nonoverlapping three blocks have only two edge candidates, both rejected by the central digits. The four remaining (g,h) are checked exhaustively for 4*9^3=2916 possibilities; the 729-entry edge census is also exhaustive. The provided standalone program passed and its independently constructed coefficient multiplication agrees across 40824 grid cases. No unproved extrapolation of finite experiments is used.

originality.rationale: OEIS A062936 supplies an explicit sufficient digit-square construction, not the converse for every three-nonzero-digit integer. Ezerman–Meyer–Solé (arXiv:1210.7593, JIS 18, Article 15.3.5) prove the expected-length no-carry case (Proposition 14), but the new claim also excludes all longer length 2d+2 palindromes in this sparse family. That exclusion needs the gap-specific carry and finite outer-block arguments, and is not implied by Proposition 14. Search comparisons did not locate an equivalent classification. An unindexed or later special-case theorem remains a risk.
residual_risks: A later or unindexed paper may have already proved a three-sparse specialization by an equivalent digit-carry argument.

value.rationale: The exact iff classification covers all positions of the middle nonzero digit and arbitrary decimal zero gaps, a complete infinite three-sparse subfamily of a published reversal-product converse conjecture. It resolves the distinctive one-digit-overflow obstruction left by the known expected-length theorem, whereas a small empirical range or the low-digit-square construction alone would not answer the structural question.
